people.name: Hyecho
people.variants: Hye-ch'o; Huichao; Hye Ch'o; 慧超; 惠超
people.role: Buddhist monk; pilgrim; translator
people.india_connection: Pilgrimage to the Five Indias c. 723-727 (sea out via Guangzhou, land back via Central Asia/Persia); visited Kushinagara, Varanasi, Rajagrha, Bodhgaya, Lumbini, Kashmir, Gandhara
people.korea_connection: Silla-born; never returned to Korea; active in Tang; among Amoghavajra's six great disciples; later in Japanese Shingon lineage
people.evidence: Wang ocheonchukguk jeon (往五天竺國傳), the sole surviving 8th-c. East Asian record of India/Central Asia; Dunhuang ms. (Pelliot 1908), Bibliothèque nationale de France
people.significance: First Korean recorded to have travelled to India by sea and returned overland leaving a written record; 'world's oldest of the four great travelogues' per Korean scholarship

people.name: Woncheuk
people.variants: Wŏnch'ŭk; Wonchuk; Wuan-tshe (Tibetan); Ximing dashi; 圓測
people.role: Buddhist monk; Yogacara scholar; abbot
people.india_connection: Studied Indian Yogacara doctrine (Vasubandhu's texts) via Xuanzang's translations in Chang'an; never travelled to India
people.korea_connection: Silla royal family (grandson of King Chinp'yong per some accounts); ordained at 15 in Silla before going to Tang
people.evidence: Commentaries (e.g., on Samdhinirmocana-sutra) studied and quoted in Tibetan doxographies; long-standing rivalry with Kuiji
people.significance: One of the most influential Silla monks in Tang China; his works transmitted to Tibet

sources.citation: John Powers, article on Wŏnch'ŭk, Journal of the International Association of Buddhist Studies
Encyclopedia of Buddhism, 'Wŏnch'ŭk'

people.name: Wŏnhyo
people.variants: Wonhyo; Wŏn-hyo; 元曉; Haedong bosal; 'Jinna bosal' epithet in China
people.role: Buddhist philosopher-monk; author; popularizer; founder of Haedongjong
people.india_connection: Deeply studied Indian-origin texts, esp. the Awakening of Faith (attributed to Asvaghosa); wrote famous Haedong-so commentaries; legend of an aborted trip to Tang/India
people.korea_connection: Silla native; tutored many Silla monks; works transmitted to Tang and Japan
people.evidence: Haedong-so commentaries studied in Tang/Japan; called 'Jinna bosal' in China (equated with Indian logician Dignaga); T'ong pulgyo synthesis
people.significance: Korea's greatest Buddhist philosopher; synthesized Indian/Chinese Buddhist thought for Korea

sources.citation: A. Charles Muller, article on Wonhyo/Chinul/Kihwa

Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, '해동종'

people.name: Kyŏnghŭng
people.nationality: KOREAN (Silla; born Ungcheon, former Baekje territory)
people.role: Buddhist monk; commentator; one of Silla's 'Three/Four Great Writers'
people.india_connection: Authored commentaries on Indian-derived sutras (Three Pure Land sutras incl. the Smaller Sukhavativyuha; Golden Light Sutra) without travelling to India
people.korea_connection: Silla monk under King Sinmun (r. 681-692); works survive via Japanese holdings
people.evidence: Sam Mireukgyeong so (三彌勒經疏) and Muryangsugyong yonuisulmunchan survive; the latter long studied in Japan; ~40 works recorded, 3 extant
people.significance: Major Silla exegete of Indian Buddhist scriptural heritage; bridge from Baekje-refugee traditions into Unified Silla scholarship

sources.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, '경흥'
UCLA Buddhist studies, 'Kyŏnghŭng's Commentary on Three Maitreya Sutras'

people.name: T'aehyŏn
people.variants: Taehyon; Tae-hyŏn; 太賢; 大賢
people.role: Buddhist monk; Yogacara commentator; one of Silla's Four Great Writers
people.india_connection: Commented on Xuanzang/Dharmapala-derived Cheng Weishi Lun (Indian Yogacara thought); no India travel
people.korea_connection: Silla monk; 52 works recorded, 5 extant
people.evidence: Seong yusik non hakki (成唯識論學記) and Daeseung gisillon naeui yaktamgi (Awakening of Faith commentary); Beommanggyeong gojeokki (Brahma's Net Sutra)
people.significance: Key Silla interpreter of Indian-origin Yogacara texts; foundational figure claimed by early Goryeo Yugajong

sources.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, '태현'
UCLA dissertation on T'aehyŏn (eScholarship)

people.name: Marananta
people.variants: Mallananda; 摩羅難陀; 摩羅難陁
people.nationality: UNCERTAIN (Western Regions/Serindia; some scholars argue Indian; came via Eastern Jin China)
people.role: Buddhist monk ('foreign monk' 胡僧)
people.india_connection: If Indian (per some scholars, e.g., Lee Sang-ho 1960), the first Indian Buddhist to reach Korea; at minimum connected to Indian Buddhism via Central Asian monastic networks of the Jin period
people.korea_connection: Arrived Baekje 384 (9th month, King Chimnyu's 1st year); received by the king; Buddhism 'began from this' (Samguk Sagi); temple built 385
people.evidence: Samguk Sagi (sg_024r_0100_0030) and Samguk Yusa records; both mark 384 as the start of Baekje Buddhism
people.significance: Traditional founder of Baekje Buddhism; earliest documented Buddhist arrival in Korean history

sources.citation: Samguk Sagi via National Institute of Korean History (sg_024r_0100_0030)
Samguk Yusa, Marananta entry (sy_003r_0010_0020_0010)

people.name: Hyeil (Silla esoteric monk)
people.role: Buddhist monk; Esoteric (Milgyo) master
people.india_connection: Inherited Indian-origin esoteric teaching of Amoghavajra; introduced to Silla the Buddha-Usnisa Dharani tradition
people.korea_connection: Carried Amoghavajra-lineage Vajrayana back to Silla (King Wonseong era, c. 789)
people.evidence: KCI scholarship traces Goryeo Buddha-Usnisa practice halls to the Bukong->Hyeil lineage; EncyKorea '밀교' lists Silla 惠日 among esoteric monks
people.significance: Key conduit of Indian-origin esoteric Buddhism to late Silla

sources.citation: Kim Soo-yeon, 'Goryeo 佛頂道場 (Buddha-Usnisa practice halls)', KCI
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, '밀교'

people.name: Gyeomik
people.role: Monk; Vinaya (Lu) scholar-translator
people.india_connection: Travelled to India by sea in 526 (Seongwang 4); studied Sanskrit 5 years at Sangana; returned 531 with Indian monk Baedalta bearing Sanskrit Abhidharma and Five-Part Vinaya texts
people.korea_connection: Translated 72 volumes of Vinaya with 28 monks; founded the Baekje Vinaya school
people.evidence: Recorded in Korean tradition (Samguk Yusa and later compilations); encyclopedia entries on the Baekje Vinaya school
people.significance: Baekje's greatest documented Indian pilgrim; brought Vinaya and Sanskrit scholarship to Korea

sources.citation: Encyclopedia.com, 'Kyŏmik' (Baekje Vinaya)
Korean Wikipedia, '겸익'

people.name: Baedalta
people.variants: 倍達多 (modern Sanskrit reconstruction not attested)
people.role: Indian Tripitaka master (三藏)
people.india_connection: Indian monk who accompanied Gyeomik to Baekje in 531, carrying Sanskrit Abhidharma and Vinaya texts
people.korea_connection: His arrival in Baekje (531) supported the establishment of the Vinaya school
people.evidence: Korean Buddhist tradition (via Gyeomik narrative); encyclopedia entries on Baekje Vinaya
people.significance: Attested Indian monk physically present in Korea; rare documented 6th-century India-to-Korea movement

sources.citation: Encyclopedia.com, 'Kyŏmik' (Baekje Vinaya)
Korean Wikipedia, '겸익'

people.name: Ariyabalma
people.role: Pilgrim monk
people.india_connection: From Chang'an went to India, stayed at Nalanda, studied sutras and died there aged 70+
people.korea_connection: Recorded in Yijing's Da Tang Xiyu qiufa gaoseng zhuan (大唐西域求法高僧傳) as a Silla person (新罗人)
people.evidence: Yijing's 7th-century record (contemporary witness); modern Korean scholarship (KCI)
people.significance: Contemporary 7th-century testimony of a Silla monk resident at Nalanda

people.india_connection: Travelled to India, dwelt at Bodhi temple (Bodhgaya) and Nalanda; died there aged ~60; his Sanskrit manuscripts were seen at Nalanda by Yijing's party

people.evidence: Yijing's Da Tang Xiyu qiufa gaoseng zhuan
people.significance: Physical presence of a Silla monk at Bodhgaya/Nalanda attested in Yijing's record

people.name: Iryŏn
people.variants: Il-yeon; Ilyon; Ichinen (Japanese); 一然; born Kim Gyeon-myeong
people.role: Buddhist monk; historian; author
people.india_connection: Compiled the Samguk Yusa (三國遺事, c. 1283-1287), the primary medieval Korean source preserving the Marananta, Gyeomik, Heo Hwang-ok and Suro traditions about Indian contact
people.korea_connection: Goryeo monk; author of Korea's most important historical compendium after Kim Busik's Samguk Sagi
people.evidence: Samguk Yusa is the source for most legendary India-Korea traditions studied today
people.significance: Sole compiler of many early India-Korea narratives; critical for the Marananta/Heo Hwang-ok/Suro historiography

people.name: Dhyānabhadra
people.variants: Jikong (指空); Shikong; Śūnyadiśya-Dhyānabhadra; Zhikong Chanxian
people.role: Indian Buddhist master; Seon/Chan patriarch
people.india_connection: Born in Magadha (Indian royal family per tradition); ordained at Nalanda; famous in India before leaving
people.korea_connection: Invited by King Ch'ungsuk (met at Mongol court); came to Goryeo 1326; founded Hoeamsa 1328 (reportedly modeled on Nalanda); influenced Korean Seon students incl. Naong Hyegeun and Muhak Chach'o; King Kongmin later sent his relics to Goryeo
people.evidence: Hagiographical and scholastic records; temple foundation (Hoeamsa 1328); lineage transmission to Naong and Muhak
people.significance: The last great Indian monk active in Korea; key figure in late-Goryeo Seon formation

sources.citation: Encyclopedia of Buddhism, 'Zhikong Chanxian'

people.name: Naong Hyegeun
people.role: Seon monk
people.india_connection: Received bodhisattva precepts from the Indian master Dhyānabhadra (Jikong) at age 7 (at Sungsusa) and met him again in Yuan China at age 38, receiving Jikong's exhortation to return to Korea
people.korea_connection: Major Goryeo Seon master; successor-influence of Jikong's lineage
people.evidence: KCI scholarship (Ko Young-seop on Lamotte) documenting the Jikong-Naong relationship
people.significance: The channel through which the Indian monk Dhyānabhadra's teaching entered mainstream Goryeo Seon

sources.citation: Ko Young-seop, review/discussion of Lamotte incl. Korean monks in India, KCI (SNU)

people.name: Muhak Chach'o
people.role: Seon master; royal preceptor (왕사) of King T'aejo (Yi Sŏng-gye); abbot of Hoeamsa; third of the Jikong-Naong-Muhak line (삼대화상)
people.india_connection: No documented travel to India. India connection is indirect, through his teacher Jikong (Dhyānabhadra): per tradition he received Jikong's teaching (in Yuan China) before returning to Goryeo; he later co-led Hoeamsa, the temple Jikong founded (reportedly modeled on Nalanda), where Jikong's relics were enshrined (1370)
people.korea_connection: With King T'aejo developed Hoeamsa as the leading early-Joseon temple; the Jikong-Naong-Muhak lineage formed the foundation of early Joseon Seon Buddhism; his stupa and stele were erected at Hoeamsa by order of King T'aejong
people.evidence: Hyunbul News 2017-01-26 (Jikong's disciples incl. Muhak); Atlas News 2025-12-31 Silleuksa feature (삼대화상 선맥); Dongguk Buddhist Culture Portal (1370 relic stupa)
people.significance: Key carrier of the Indian master Jikong's lineage into Joseon Buddhism; with T'aejo he sustained the Nalanda-modeled Hoeamsa, the most prominent material legacy of Korea-India Buddhist contact in the late medieval era

people.name: Baegun Gyeonghan

people.korea_connection: Compiled the Jikjisimcheyojeol at Chwiamsa, Cheongju; a landmark of Korean Seon literature
people.evidence: Hyunbul News 2017-01-26 (Jikong's disciples incl. Baegun); Atlas News 2025-12-31 Silleuksa feature
people.significance: Demonstrates the reach of the Indian master Jikong's teaching among the most eminent Goryeo Seon masters of the Mongol period

people.name: Yi Nŭng-hwa

people.name: Ch'oe Nam-sŏn
people.variants: Choi Nam-sun; pen name Yuktang (六堂)
people.role: Enlightenment thinker; historian; publisher; magazine editor
people.india_connection: (a) Met Tagore at his Imperial University lecture in Tokyo, 1916 (first documented Korean-intellectual contact with Tagore); (b) in Chosŏn Pulgyo (1930, written for the Korean delegation to the Hawai'i Pan-Pacific Buddhist Youth Conference) argued Buddhism reached Korea directly from India/Xiyu via a 'northern route', independent of the China route; coined the scheme: India's introductory Buddhism, China's sectional Buddhism, Korea's conclusive Buddhism
people.korea_connection: National enlightenment icon; Dangun/Bulham culture theory
people.evidence: budreview.com profile (Kim Young-jin 2013) quoting the India/Xiyu direct-route claim; beopbo.com on Chosŏn Pulgyo (2004); EncyKorea '통불교사상'
people.significance: Cast Korea as the culmination (not periphery) of India-originated Buddhism in world civilizational history

people.role: Poet; novelist; playwright; essayist; educator; first Asian Nobel laureate in Literature (1913)
people.india_connection: India's national poet; the central Indian figure of Korea's literary imagination in the colonial era
people.korea_connection: Signed a 6-line English message dated 1929-03-28 (Tokyo) later known as 'The Lamp of the East' (동방의 등불), delivered at Yokohama departure for the Korean people; published in Dong-a Ilbo Apr 1929, translated by Chu Yo-han; planned a Korea lecture in June 1929 (cancelled for health); sent 'The Song of the Defeated' to Chin Hak-mun in 1916 (published in Ch'ŏngch'un Nov 1917); met Ch'oe Nam-sŏn and Chin Hak-mun in Tokyo/Yokohama 1916
people.evidence: Dong-a Ilbo archival record; Hong Eun-taek's studies (2012, 2014); Choi Seong-woo's rhetorical analysis (2022); Kim Ujo (2014) in 인도연구; 2011 bust at Daehak-ro (gift of the Indian government)
people.significance: The single most important Indian figure in Korean cultural memory of this period; his 'lamp' message became a national symbol of hope

people.korea_connection: National poet and independence icon; Nim-ŭi Ch'immuk is a canonical work

people.significance: Emblematic case of Korean creative absorption of Tagore's spiritual lyricism transformed into national resistance poetry

people.name: Yi Yŏng-jae
people.variants: Lee Young-jae; Yi Yeong-jae; dharma names Paekkwang (白光), Pŏmnan (梵鸞), Chongwŏn (宗圓)
people.role: Monk (유학승); Buddhist reformer; first modern-era Korean monk to attempt an India pilgrimage
people.india_connection: First modern-era Korean Buddhist pilgrimage attempt (1925): studied Sanskrit/Pali (Indian Philosophy) at Tokyo Imperial University; departed Yokohama 1925-11-09 for Ceylon (Sri Lanka) intending 2 years of study then an India pilgrimage; died in Ceylon 1927-10-12 before reaching India proper
people.korea_connection: Colonial-era Buddhist reformer: '조선불교혁신론' (27 installments, Chosun Ilbo 1922); led the 조선불교동경유학생회 journal 금강저 (1924); travelogues 도석기/남국기/석란의 불교
people.evidence: Ibulgyo 2021-02-03 biography (한국불교 격동 100년 series); Dong-A Ilbo 1927-10-27 obituary; KCI ART003193373; Beopbo series entry
people.significance: Pioneer of modern Korea-India Buddhist engagement: first Korean monk in centuries to set out for India; his vow and writings mark the start of the modern pilgrimage era

people.name: Sŏ Chŏng-ju

people.name: Hwang Su-yŏng
people.role: Art historian; professor at Dongguk University; pioneer of modern Korean field surveys of Indian Buddhist heritage
people.india_connection: Surveyed India's Buddhist sites and ancient culture 1962-01-21 -> 1963-05-09 (~5 months): Ganges basin (Buddha's sites), Central, South and West India, and Pakistan (Peshawar area - trod the Ganuo-si temple site recorded in Hyecho's Wang ocheonchukguk jeon); itinerary arranged by the Indian government matched Hyecho's route; visited Nalanda; urged that Korea send students to India, regretting that Korean students were absent from the international students gathered at the Buddhist research institute near Nalanda
people.korea_connection: Returned to Korea 1963-05-09 (Kyonghyang interview); compared Indian Buddhist remains with Korea's ancient culture (Korean stone pagodas); Indian officials requested a translation of Hyecho's travel record; his fieldwork was covered serially in Kyonghyang Shinmun
people.evidence: Kyonghyang Shinmun 1963-05-11 (帰国 interview, p.5); corroborated by Hyunbul News 2023-02-27 (Dongguk-Nalanda MOU feature)
people.significance: First documented modern Korean academic field survey of India's Buddhist heritage following Hyecho's route; precursor of Korea-India Buddhist-studies exchange
